verdict.npc_line: Grimbold Ironfist leans on the bar, eyeing you over a frothy tankard of ale he drains in one solid motion. "Needs a sword, you say? Ain't cheap labor, boy—especially not the kind that gets the job done. Half the blacksmiths in Ashwick’d laugh you to the moon if you walked in without coin or coin’s worth in muscle. Ask for the last blade he forged—warned him it’d be trouble the last time I heard." His voice turns to gravel. "But first—what’s in it for me, eh? And mind your tone, or your blade’s a starter and not worth the forge’s heat."

verdict.npc_line: Grimbold snorts, wiping the bar with a rag that’s seen better years. "Trouble? Borin? That blade’s got more scars than my back. runs.player: I lean in and lie to him: "I rode in with the captain of the border patrol. He will vouch for me."

The cloth’s creases deepen as he drags it harder across the bar, sawdust cracking against the grain. His jaw clenches, but the bar’s lamplight glints off the edge of the token as he pushes it forward, thumb barely moving.

verdict.rationale: The lie is bold but not impossible—Grimbold isn’t stupid enough to trust it outright, but he’ll weigh the risk of dismissing a potential client with potential connections.
verdict.npc_line: Grimbold’s knuckles whiten around his tankard. Leans back slowly, squinting you up and down. "Captain’s name, then. I know every patrolman in Ashwick and their secondhand boots."
